flags.message: gemini-baseline, codex-baseline, and claude-baseline all report a blank 44-page application extraction at prediction time. The evaluator's current document manifest marks it empty_text=false and ocr_derived=true, and the current application.txt is 50,786 bytes. The candidate-time document version is not staged, so the current OCR availability cannot verify what each candidate could read. Evaluations honor the disclosed earlier text gap and do not penalize it or use the current body to reconstruct the candidates' evidence. This is an input-provenance limitation, not evidence of leakage or an evaluation blocker.

All three candidates report that at their 2026-10-03 run the provisioned application (44 pages, fetched 2026-10-03) carried empty_text: true and a blank application.txt, so every prediction was made from the docket line and caption alone. The record staged for this evaluation now carries an OCR-derived body (documents.json: empty_text false, ocr_derived true) showing a Texas child-custody conservatorship modification and writ of attachment, with the appeal dismissed below for nonpayment of a $205 fee. Not a defect in any candidate; recorded so the OCR fallback's timing relative to the predict fan-out is visible to maintainers, since one candidate's subject-matter inference (landlord-tenant or civil-rights) was wrong for want of the text.

Salience version mismatch: the predictions froze a band under `sal-v3`, but the committed statpack.md provides `sal-v4` bands. Per the rules, segment_base_rate and brier_skill_score have been omitted.

gemini-baseline, claude-baseline, and codex-baseline freeze band baseline under sal-v3 for Term 2026, but the committed metrics/statpack.md segment table is headed sal-v4. Per the evaluation contract, segment_base_rate and brier_skill_score are omitted and base_rate_basis is null for all three. A frozen band cannot use the terminal fallback. Outcome correctness and Brier scores are unaffected; individual evaluation.md files explain the unavailable baseline.

Salience-version mismatch on every candidate (gemini-baseline, claude-baseline, codex-baseline): each prediction froze band 'baseline' under salience_version 'sal-v3', while the committed metrics/statpack.md renders the 'Segment base rate by salience band' table under 'sal-v4'. Per the evaluate prompt the table is no baseline for that band, so segment_base_rate and brier_skill_score are omitted and base_rate_basis is null on all three evaluation.json files. Note for the stamp: statpack.json still carries a sal-v3 alt_segments block (OT2017-OT2025; baseline-band reached figures pool to ~5.0% over n~12,720), so the harness's version-pinned pooling may resolve a claim baseline even though the rendered table cannot. The evaluator-written trio is left null as the prompt's only sanctioned answer.

codex-baseline's retrieval.md discloses three CourtListener MCP searches that failed with HTTP 429, but its captured retrieval_log.json (29 calls, coverage 1.0) carries no mcp call class; the only non-shell rows are two 'other' entries whose text the harness redacted as credential-shaped. The disclosed calls are therefore unobserved in the log. Not a leakage concern (forward cell, searches named companion cases only); noted because the staged log and the candidate's own disclosure cannot be reconciled from the blinded view.

Forward-cell timing relative to the conference order lists: all three candidates ran on 2026-10-04, after the 2026-10-01 grant list from the 2026-09-28 conference had issued and one day before the 2026-10-05 denial. A petition absent from the grant list is, at that point, almost certainly a denial or a relist, so a forward cell placed in that window carries a strong legitimate signal about its own disposition that the band baseline does not condition on. claude-baseline disclosed seeing other 2026-10-01 grants in a corpus query and did not look for this case; none of the three used the signal. Not leakage under the mode rules, but worth weighing in how forward distribution-moment cells are scheduled against the Court's order-list calendar.

The blinded prediction.json stages big_case_score and big_case_rationale alongside the fields the evaluator must read first, so the instruction to form the big_case read before seeing the predictor's cannot be honoured structurally. My read (0.42) was formed from the record and outcome and I did not use the predictors' values, but the independence is procedural rather than enforced.

The frozen context for codex-baseline, claude-baseline and gemini-baseline carries distribution_count 2 and elevated/sal-v4. The provisioned October 5 snapshot links 25M81 and records a May 19 distribution followed by June 8 'Motion Denied.', then the August response waiver and August 26 distribution. The first distribution may concern the veteran-status motion rather than substantive cert consideration. This is a motion/petition signal ambiguity, not a finding that the recorded count is wrong. Please review event attribution; all evaluations preserve the frozen elevated risk-set baseline and recorded outcome without editing either.

gemini-baseline's retrieval note states no retrieval beyond provisioned inputs, but its harness log contains 'fedcourts query --court scotus --era 2020s'. All 26 results are unobserved, so the query's success, returned content and transfer amount cannot be established. The note omits a visible attempt; this is not proof of undisclosed successful retrieval or leakage. Evaluation.md preserves that distinction and does not treat the uncaptured result as empty.

The frozen context and outcome both carry distribution_count 2 (dist-v2), but the snapshot's two DISTRIBUTED entries belong to different filings: the May 19 distribution (conference 6/4) was of the petitioner's motion for leave to proceed as a veteran under the linked docket 25M81, denied June 8, and only the August 26 distribution (conference 9/28) was of the petition itself. The petition was therefore a never-relisted paid petition at its first conference, while the count (and plausibly the elevated sal-v4 band) read it as twice-distributed. Scored against the frozen band as the contract requires; noting so the parser or scorer can decide whether a motion-docket distribution should count toward the petition's trajectory.

The candidates' quoted anchor (6.55%, n~13,163) came from the table as rendered on 2026-08-16; the current pack pools to 5.02%, a vintage difference, not an arithmetic error.

Arrival-moment cell provisioned from a snapshot dated 2026-08-16, 26 days after docketing (2026-07-21). The snapshot already carried the linked stay application 26A145 (filed Jul 24, denied by Justice Kagan Aug 3, refiled Aug 6) and an Aug 11 supplemental brief; two candidates used the single-Justice stay denial as a negative signal and one explicitly set it aside. This is legitimate forward information, not leakage (distribution_count was still 0), but it is a docket-acquired signal inside a cell defined as 'before any docket-acquired signal exists'. Separately, the docket's petition entry is dated Dec 30 2025 while DocketedDate is July 21, 2026 and the PDF path is dated 2026-07-24; one candidate noted the inconsistency.

All results are unobserved, so success, returned material, and transfer counts cannot be established. This is a retrieval-accounting discrepancy, not evidence of outcome leakage; the forward calls preceded the October 5 disposition.

The provisioned petition has a March 23, 2026 filing stamp but a June 2026 signature, while the snapshot records July 17 docketing after January 6 rehearing denial. The chronology is unresolved, not proof of untimeliness. claude-baseline acknowledges the inconsistency but incorrectly says either filing-date reading is within 90 days: March 23 is 76 days after January 6; even June 1 is 146 days later. Scores retain the recorded October 5 denial. See evaluation.md for the reasoning-quality consequence; no outcome leakage is inferred.
